classification.difficultyReason: Select four different congruence tests from marked diagrams, recognise shared sides and preserve matching vertex order.

content.prompt: In each part, write a congruence statement, giving a congruence test as the reason. Make sure that you name the vertices in matching order.

spec.description: Kite divided by the common segment AB; double ticks on AP and AQ and single ticks on PB and QB. Decorative source blue is rendered black.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; no congruence statement supplied.

answer.worked:
In triangles $ABP$ and $ABQ$:
$$\begin{aligned}AP&=AQ &&\text{(given)}\\BP&=BQ &&\text{(given)}\\AB&=AB &&\text{(common)}\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $\triangle ABP\equiv\triangle ABQ$ (SSS).

spec.description: Two separate triangles side by side, retaining their different orientations, right angles, 60-degree labels and matching side ticks.
spec.mathematics: Angle F=angle N=90 degrees; angle A=angle T=60 degrees; FG=NL.

answer.worked:
In triangles $FAG$ and $NTL$:
$$\begin{aligned}\angle AFG&=\angle TNL=90^\circ &&\text{(given)}\\\angle FAG&=\angle NTL=60^\circ &&\text{(given)}\\FG&=NL &&\text{(given)}\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $\triangle FAG\equiv\triangle NTL$ (AAS).

spec.description: Quadrilateral P Q R S divided by PR, with right angles at Q and S and matching double ticks on PQ and SR.
spec.mathematics: PR is the common hypotenuse; PQ=RS; angle PQR=angle RSP=90 degrees.

answer.worked:
In right-angled triangles $PQR$ and $RSP$:
$$\begin{aligned}\angle PQR&=\angle RSP=90^\circ &&\text{(given)}\\PR&=RP &&\text{(common hypotenuse)}\\PQ&=RS &&\text{(given)}\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $\triangle PQR\equiv\triangle RSP$ (RHS).

spec.description: B, C and A are collinear in that order. CD divides triangle BAD; BC and CA have double ticks and the right-angle square lies between CB and CD.
spec.mathematics: AC=BC; CD is common; both angles at C are right angles because BA is straight and CD is perpendicular to it.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source right-angle square is drawn; the supplementary right angle is inferred in the solution.

answer.worked:
$A$, $C$ and $B$ lie on a straight line, so $\angle ACD=180^\circ-90^\circ=90^\circ$.

In triangles $ACD$ and $BCD$:
$$\begin{aligned}AC&=BC &&\text{(given)}\\\angle ACD&=\angle BCD=90^\circ\\CD&=CD &&\text{(common)}\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $\triangle ACD\equiv\triangle BCD$ (SAS).
